title: deterministic-tool-provenance-and-priority-resolver-for-openai-compat
author: Ava Moreno
description:
Motivation:
Users observed non-deterministic tool selection across retries and streaming fragments when the OpenAI compatibility layer synthesized tool_choice decisions. This caused duplicate tool invocations and confusing assistant/tool provenance in logs. The goal of this PR is to provide a deterministic, monotonic priority resolver for tool discovery, attach lightweight provenance to tool selection decisions, and preserve stream fragment boundaries and message metadata so clients can rehydrate continuous tool calls without ambiguity.

What this change does (single-line narrative): Adds a compatibility shim that maps OpenAI-style function/tool schemas into an internal priority-annotated catalog, enforces deterministic selection policy across retries/fallbacks, and ensures streaming fragments carry explicit fragment markers and provenance tags for tool messages.

Details/Approach:
- Tool priority mapping: introduce a stable priority vector derived from (explicit tool priority annotation if present, tool confidence heuristics, and deterministic tie-breaker based on tool_id canonical order). This ensures identical input + catalog state yields the same tool_choice.
- Provenance envelope: selected tool invocations now include a small provenance header (tool_selector_version, selection_score, selection_reason) that travels in both the stream meta and the non-streaming invoke envelope. This lets downstream consumers attribute outputs to a specific selection decision and facilitates replay.
- Streaming fragment preservation: framed streaming chunks now include fragment_id and fragment_index headers for tool messages. We preserve fragment boundary markers when coalescing or splitting fragments during network retransmit/rebuffer.
- Schema mapping changes: extend openai compat mapper to preserve optional param_aliases and required/optional field qualifiers in the translated internal schema to reduce accidental silent failures on strict tool runtimes.
- Retry/fallback semantics: when a fallback model or stub is used we attach selection_reason annotated as "fallback-route" and keep the original selection_score to make post-hoc analysis straightforward.

Files changed (high-level):
- src/compat/openai/tool_priority_resolver.rs: new deterministic priority logic and tie-breaker utilities.
- src/compat/openai/tool_provenance.rs: provenance envelope generator and serializer.
- src/serving/stream/framing.rs: add fragment_id, fragment_index headers and coalescing logic.
- api/openai_compat/README.md: spec notes on new provenance headers and fragment markers.
- tests/integration/tool_choice_replay.test.ts: deterministic replay + fragment reassembly tests.
- tests/unit/tool_priority.test.rs: coverage for tie-breakers and score stability.
- docs/release/notes/2026-02-26-tool-provenance.md: release notes.

Commits (summary):
- feat(compat): add deterministic tool priority resolver and utilities
- feat(compat): add provenance envelope and serializer
- fix(stream): preserve fragment headers during coalesce/split
- test: add integration tests for replay and fragment reassembly
- docs: update openai_compat README and release notes

Testing and validation:
- Unit test suite covers canonical tie-breaker ordering and selection stability across simulated catalog reorders.
- Integration tests replay the same request over a randomized catalog ordering and assert identical tool_choice and identical provenance headers.
- End-to-end streaming test validates fragment reassembly and idempotent-invoke behavior when client reconnects mid-stream.
- Ran internal performance benchmark: added ~0.6ms median overhead on selection path (within SLO), no measurable impact on token throughput for steady-state batched loads.

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Compatibility: all old invocations still function; we only add extra metadata fields (provenance headers and fragment markers). Clients that ignore these will see no behavioral change.
- Migration: operators that relied on implicit nondeterminism should be aware that tool selection is now deterministic by default; an opt-out env var (OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_UNORDERED) is provided for a short transitional window.

Checklist:
- [x] New unit tests
- [x] Integration tests (replay + streaming)
- [x] Docs and release notes
- [x] Perf smoke test

Related tickets: Linear ENG-2104 (deterministic tool routing), ENG-2147 (stream fragment metadata), SUP-7821 (support case: duplicate tool calls during reconnect)

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the tie-breaker logic in tool_priority_resolver.rs (stable sort is critical) and the fragment coalescer change — I added comments where we preserve original fragment boundaries.
commits_summary: 5 commits: deterministic resolver, provenance serializer, stream framing updates, tests, docs
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice isolation between resolver and mapper. Please add a short comment explaining why we pick tool_id canonical order as the final tie-breaker.
Elena Soto: Can we add a debug flag to emit full selection_score breakdown in debug logs? It will help support investigations.
Marcus Li: Streaming reassembly looks good; one nit on off-by-one in fragment_index when coalescing two fragments.
Ava Moreno (author): Addressed Marcus' off-by-one nit and added a unit test; added a small comment about canonical order and flag to enable verbose selection logs behind a feature gate.
release_notes: Added deterministic tool priority resolver and provenance headers for OpenAI compatibility layer. Streaming fragments for tool messages now include fragment_id/fragment_index. No behavioral breaking changes; opt-out available via OPENAI_COMPAT_ALLOW_UNORDERED.
notes_for_ops: Operators should roll forward without downtime. If you have custom tooling parsing tool_choice text blobs, update parsers to read the new provenance headers. Enable fallback logging for a day to verify selection stability in production.
extra_context: This PR intentionally keeps selection math deterministic to make post-hoc analysis and auditing simpler; will follow up with a separate PR to expose selection telemetry to Redwood Console as per ENG-2210.
